mainTopic: End of פרק האשה נקנית and the opening of האיש מקדש: doing קידושין in person or through a שליח, marrying off a daughter, and the Torah source for שליחות
overview: The amud opens with the last lines of פרק האשה נקנית. An angry person gains nothing but his anger, a good person tastes the fruit of his deeds, and someone with no מקרא, no משנה and no דרך ארץ should be avoided. After the הדרן, the new פרק, האיש מקדש, begins with a משנה: a man or a woman can do קידושין personally or through a שליח, and a father can marry off his daughter who is a נערה. The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say 'by himself.' רב יוסף answers that doing a מצוה yourself is better, like רב ספרא and רבא, who prepared their own food for שבת. A second version says a man using a שליח is actually forbidden, because רב rules that a man must see a woman before marrying her (ואהבת לרעך כמוך). In that version, רב יוסף's teaching applies only to the woman, who would rather be married than alone (ריש לקיש). The משנה's words 'when she is a נערה' support רב's ruling that a father should not marry off a קטנה. The גמרא then finds the source for שליחות in the פסוקים about a גט, and extends it to קידושין through the היקש of ויצאה and והיתה. The amud ends by bringing a משנה about a שליח separating תרומה; the question it sets up continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Anger gets you nothing; goodness bears fruit
steps.stepSummary: The closing teaching of the פרק continues: the angry person ends up with nothing but anger, while a good person gets to taste the fruit of his deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gets nothing out of it except his anger. And a good person is allowed to taste the fruit of his good deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching about character that started on the previous page. It sets the angry person against the good person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anger brings no gain. In the end the angry person is left holding only the anger itself. The good person is the opposite: his deeds produce real results, and he gets to enjoy them.

keyTerms.meaning: The fruit, meaning the results, of his deeds

phrases.english: He has gained nothing except anger.
phrases.notes: This saying started on the previous page. 'He' is the angry person.

phrases.english: And a good person is given a taste
of the fruit of his deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an אגדה teaching from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anger brings no benefit. Good deeds bring rewards the good person gets to enjoy.

steps.title: Stay away from someone with no Torah and no decent conduct
steps.stepSummary: Someone who has no מקרא, no משנה and no דרך ארץ should be avoided, even to the point of vowing not to benefit from him. A פסוק in תהלים supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who is not involved in Bible, nor in משנה, nor in proper conduct: vow not to benefit from him. As the פסוק says, 'nor sat in the seat of scorners.' His seat is a seat of scorners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final teaching: a person with no Torah learning and no proper behavior is someone to keep away from. It brings a פסוק as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three things listed are מקרא, משנה and דרך ארץ. Someone who has none of them is spending his life on empty matters. The פסוק calls that the 'seat of scorners,' so the good person stays away from him.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה, the oral Torah teachings
The seat of scorners, a gathering of mockers

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק ends with a values lesson: a life with no Torah and no decent conduct is a 'seat of scorners,' and one should keep away from it.

phrases.english: And anyone who is not involved in Bible,
nor in משנה, nor in proper conduct –
vow not to benefit from him,
as it says: 'nor sat in the seat of scorners' –
his seat is a seat of scorners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא בַּמִּקְרָא וְלֹא בַּמִּשְׁנָה וְלֹא בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing teaching to the character theme
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid benefiting from someone with no מקרא, no משנה and no דרך ארץ, since his seat is a 'seat of scorners.'

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק האשה נקנית
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line of the first פרק of קידושין, האשה נקנית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'האשה נקנית.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the first פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said when finishing a פרק, expressing the hope to come back and learn it again. The next line begins a brand new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A woman is acquired,' the name of the first פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'A woman is acquired'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that the previous steps ended
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of קידושין is complete.

steps.title: משנה: betrothing in person or through an agent
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens: a man can do קידושין himself or through a שליח. A woman can accept קידושין herself or through a שליח. A father can marry off his daughter who is a נערה, himself or through a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man can betroth a woman himself or through his agent. A woman can be betrothed herself or through her agent. A man can betroth his daughter when she is a נערה, himself or through his agent.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the opening משנה of the second פרק. It teaches that קידושין can be done in person or through an agent, by the man, by the woman, and by a father for his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three cases where a שליח works: the man giving קידושין, the woman accepting it, and a father accepting it for his daughter while she is a נערה. In each case the משנה mentions both options, 'himself' and 'his agent.'

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl just past childhood, still under her father's authority

steps.confusionAlert: Don't skip over the words 'by himself' (בו). They look obvious, but the גמרא is about to ask exactly why they are there.

phrases.english: A man betroths by himself or through his agent.
A woman becomes betrothed by herself or through her agent.

phrases.aramaic: הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה,
phrases.english: A man betroths his daughter when she is a נערה,
phrases.notes: He means the father accepts קידושין on her behalf, marrying her off to someone.

phrases.english: by himself or through his agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין can be done personally or through a שליח, by the man, the woman, or a father for his נערה daughter.

steps.title: Why mention 'by himself' at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if even an agent can do קידושין, it's obvious that the man himself can. Why does the משנה say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now that he can betroth through his agent, is it really necessary to say he can betroth by himself?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. The words 'by himself' seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent only acts on behalf of the man. So if the agent's act works, the man's own act should surely work. The משנה doesn't waste words, so the 'extra' phrase needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה

phrases.english: גמרא: Now that he betroths through his agent,
is it necessary to say by himself?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'בו' (by himself) in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic: if an agent works, the man himself surely does, so the phrase seems extra.

steps.title: Doing the מצוה yourself is better
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the משנה is teaching a preference: it is a bigger מצוה to do קידושין yourself than through an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is a greater מצוה to do it himself than through his agent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why 'by himself' is in the משנה. It teaches that doing it personally is the better way to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף agrees that both ways work. The extra words don't teach whether it is valid. They teach which way is preferred: the מצוה is done best by the man himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a greater מצוה to do it yourself than through your agent

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle: even when a שליח is allowed, a person should try to do a מצוה himself.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
It is a greater מצוה by himself than through his agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף מִצְוָה בּוֹ יוֹתֵר מִבִּשְׁלוּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra words
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra words teach a preference, not whether the act is valid
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since an agent works, saying 'by himself' adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both work, but doing it yourself is the greater מצוה.

steps.title: Examples: רב ספרא and רבא prepared food themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רב יוסף's idea with how great חכמים personally did work for a מצוה: רב ספרא singed a head, and רבא salted a fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב ספרא, who would singe the head of an animal, and רבא, who would salt a שיבוטא fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings real-life examples of חכמים who did a מצוה with their own hands, even though others could have done it for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These were important people who could easily have sent someone else. They chose to do the work themselves, which shows the same idea as רב יוסף's rule: a מצוה done in person is greater.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's rule (מצוה בו יותר מבשלוחו) is shown in practice by רב ספרא and רבא, who did their own preparation work for a מצוה.

phrases.english: Like that of רב ספרא,
who would singe the head,
phrases.notes: This was his own preparation of food for שבת.

phrases.english: and רבא would salt a שיבוטא fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב סָפְרָא מְחָרֵיךְ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports רב יוסף's answer
steps.raayaObject: The principle that doing a מצוה yourself is greater than doing it through an agent
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב ספרא and רבא, who prepared food with their own hands

steps.title: Second version: a man using an agent is actually forbidden
steps.stepSummary: According to איכא דאמרי, a man doing קידושין through a שליח involves an איסור. This is based on רב's rule that a man must see a woman before he marries her, because of ואהבת לרעך כמוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: here there is even a prohibition. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: a man may not marry a woman until he sees her. Otherwise he might find something about her he doesn't like and come to dislike her, and the Torah says, 'Love your neighbor as yourself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the discussion. In this version, a man sending a שליח is not just a smaller מצוה. It is actually forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, sending a שליח was only less preferred. Now רב's rule raises it to an איסור: a man must see his bride first, so he won't marry someone he will later dislike. This means רב יוסף's 'bigger מצוה' idea can't be about the man's part of the משנה. The next step moves it somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: Unappealing, something he would find unpleasant

steps.confusionAlert: איכא דאמרי does not argue about the law of רב ספרא and רבא. It is a different version of where רב יוסף's statement was said: on the woman's part of the משנה, not the man's part.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a man should see a woman before marrying her.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
in this case there is also a prohibition,
phrases.notes: 'This case' means a man doing קידושין through a שליח.

phrases.english: like what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
For רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
It is forbidden for a man to betroth a woman
until he sees her,
in case he sees something unappealing in her
and she becomes distasteful to him,
and the Merciful One said:
"And you shall love your neighbor as yourself."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בְּהָא אִיסּוּרָא נָמֵי אִית בֵּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version that turns 'less of a מצוה' into an actual איסור for a man who uses a שליח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man may not marry a woman through a שליח without seeing her, because he might come to dislike her and go against ואהבת לרעך כמוך.

steps.title: The question moves to the woman's part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רב יוסף's statement was said on the second part of the משנה. Since a woman can accept קידושין through her שליח, why does the משנה need to say she can do it herself?
steps.simpleTranslation: And when רב יוסף's statement was said, it was said on the later part: 'A woman can be betrothed herself or through her agent.' If she can be betrothed even through her agent, is it necessary to say she can do it herself?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves the 'it's obvious' question from the man to the woman. This sets up רב יוסף's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's part of the משנה is already explained by רב's איסור, so the question can't be asked there anymore. But the woman's part still seems to say something obvious. That is where רב יוסף's question and answer now belong.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה
Now (used to mean: if even this is true...)

phrases.english: And when רב יוסף's statement was said,
it was said about the later part of the משנה:
A woman can be betrothed by herself or through her agent.
Now, if she can be betrothed through her agent,
is it necessary to say she can by herself?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the man's part is now explained by the איסור, the 'obvious' question moves to the woman's part.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words that a woman can be betrothed by herself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a שליח works, then of course she can do it herself, so the words seem unnecessary.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is a bigger מצוה for the woman herself
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that for the woman, it is a bigger מצוה to accept קידושין herself. He backs this up with רב ספרא and רבא personally doing work for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is a bigger מצוה for her to do it herself than through her agent. This is like רב ספרא, who singed an animal's head himself, and רבא, who salted a fish himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The same answer from רב יוסף, and the same support, now explain the woman's part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman, using a שליח is allowed, but doing it herself is a bigger מצוה. That is why the משנה mentions 'herself.' The stories of רב ספרא and רבא show that great people did a מצוה's work with their own hands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a bigger מצוה to do it herself
Singes the head of an animal

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
It is a bigger מצוה to do it herself than through her agent.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב סָפְרָא מְחָרֵיךְ רֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: Like רב ספרא, who would singe a head,
and רבא, who would salt a fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִצְוָה בָּהּ יוֹתֵר מִבִּשְׁלוּחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the woman's part using רב יוסף's idea of a bigger מצוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The words teach that doing it herself is preferred
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'by herself' seem to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a woman, accepting קידושין herself is a bigger מצוה than using a שליח.

steps.title: Why a woman using an agent is not forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A woman's שליח involves no איסור, because of ריש לקיש's saying: a woman would rather be married than alone, so she won't come to dislike her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, with the woman, there is no prohibition, like ריש לקיש said: 'Better to sit as two than to sit as a widow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב's worry about not seeing the other person applies to a man but not to a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's איסור comes from the worry that the person will later dislike their spouse. ריש לקיש says a woman would rather be married than alone, so she will be satisfied anyway. Since there is no worry, there is no איסור for her, only a bigger מצוה to do it herself.
steps.whatToRemember: In this version: a man may not marry through a שליח without seeing the woman (איסור). A woman may use a שליח, but doing it herself is a bigger מצוה.

phrases.english: But in this case there is no prohibition,
phrases.notes: 'This case' means a woman accepting קידושין through her שליח.

phrases.english: like what ריש לקיש said,
for ריש לקיש said:
It is better to sit as two bodies
than to sit as a widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּהָא אִיסּוּרָא לֵית בַּהּ, כִּדְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב's איסור does not apply to the woman, so רב יוסף's 'bigger מצוה' fits her case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the reason for the איסור is missing in the woman's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רב's איסור applies to a woman too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman is happy to be married, so she won't come to dislike her husband, and there is no איסור.

steps.title: Reading the משנה: a father marries off a daughter who is a נערה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's last part and reads it closely: it says 'when she is a נערה,' so this is allowed for a נערה but not for a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A man can betroth his daughter when she is a נערה.' When she is a נערה, yes. When she is a קטנה, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last part of the משנה and learns something from its exact words. This sets up a support for רב in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just said 'a father can marry off his daughter.' Adding 'when she is a נערה' suggests that he should not do it when she is a קטנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl just past 12 who has shown signs of maturity (still under her father's authority for a short time)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean a father cannot legally marry off a קטנה. By Torah law he can, and the קידושין work. The point is that he should not do so in the first place.

phrases.aramaic: הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה.
phrases.english: A man can betroth his daughter when she is a young woman.
When she is a young woman, yes;
when she is a minor, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה – אִין, כְּשֶׁהִיא קְטַנָּה – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the man and woman parts of the משנה to the father's part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's words suggest a father should marry off his daughter as a נערה, not as a קטנה.

steps.title: This supports רב: wait until she grows up and chooses
steps.stepSummary: The close reading of the משנה supports רב (or רבי אלעזר): a father may not marry off his daughter as a קטנה. He must wait until she grows up and says whom she wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב. רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say it was רבי אלעזר: a man may not betroth his daughter while she is a קטנה. He must wait until she grows up and says, 'I want so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה's wording backs up רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה hinted that marrying off a קטנה is not done. רב states it outright as an איסור, and gives the reason: she must be old enough to choose her husband herself. So the משנה supports רב.
steps.whatToRemember: A father should not marry off his daughter while she is a קטנה. He must wait until she can choose for herself. This matches the idea from step 8 that people should not marry someone they may come to dislike.

phrases.english: This supports רב,
for רב יהודה said in the name of רב,
and some say it was רבי אלעזר:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיְּקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא קְטַנָּה,
phrases.english: It is forbidden for a man to betroth his daughter when she is a minor,
until she grows up and says:
"I want so-and-so."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the close reading from step 12 to support רב's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a father may not marry off a קטנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'when she is a נערה'

steps.title: What is the source for agency?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a שליח can act for someone.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that agency works?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה said a man or woman can do קידושין through a שליח, so the גמרא now asks where the Torah teaches that agency works at all. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the גמרא simply assumed that a שליח works. Now it wants a Torah source for the whole idea of שליחות.

keyTerms.meaning: Agency, where one person acts on behalf of another
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: From where do we know agency?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's rule that קידושין can be done through a שליח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the source for the שליח mentioned in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source for the concept of שליחות.

steps.title: Agency is learned from the verses about divorce
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״וְשִׁלַּח״ and ״וְשִׁלְּחָהּ״ that the husband, the wife, and even a שליח can appoint an agent for a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: ״וְשִׁלַּח״ teaches that he can appoint a שליח. ״וְשִׁלְּחָהּ״ teaches that she can appoint a שליח. Saying both ״וְשִׁלַּח״ and ״וְשִׁלְּחָהּ״ teaches that a שליח can appoint another שליח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns three rules about agency from the words of the גט פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for 'send' (שלח) has the same root as שליח. So the husband can send a שליח with the גט. Reading ״וְשִׁלְּחָהּ״ as 'and she sends' teaches that the wife can appoint a שליח to receive it. The repeated wording teaches that a שליח can appoint another שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: And he sends her (can also be read 'and she sends')

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the basic Torah source for שליחות. All three rules (husband, wife, and a שליח appointing a שליח) come from the פסוקים about a גט.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "And he sends"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1, about a man divorcing his wife.

phrases.english: teaches that he can appoint an agent.
"And he sends her" teaches
phrases.notes: Without vowels, these same letters can also be read as 'and she sends.'

phrases.english: that she can appoint an agent.
The extra "and he sends" and "and he sends her"
teaches that an agent can appoint another agent.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words ״וְשִׁלַּח״ and ״וְשִׁלְּחָהּ״ in the פסוקים about a גט teach agency for the husband, for the wife, and for a שליח appointing another שליח.

steps.title: How do we know agency works for betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: The source only covers גירושין. We cannot learn קידושין from it, because a גט can be given against the woman's will.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for divorce. From where do we know it for betrothal? And if you say we learn it from divorce, that does not work: divorce is special, because it can happen against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא only spoke about גירושין, and it asks for a source for קידושין. It also shuts down the easy answer of copying the rule from גירושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Divorce has a 'stronger' quality, since a man can divorce his wife even if she does not agree. So maybe agency only works for something that strong. קידושין needs her agreement, so we cannot simply assume the same rule applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? It is different, because...

steps.confusionAlert: ״מָה לְגֵירוּשִׁין״ is not a new question. It is the גמרא knocking down the idea of learning קידושין from גירושין by pointing out a difference between them.

phrases.english: We found it for divorce;
from where do we know it for betrothal?
And if you say it is learned from divorce,
what about divorce? It is special,
since it can happen against her will!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the source in step 15 only covers גירושין, so a source for קידושין is still missing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that agency works for קידושין, since it cannot simply be learned from גירושין.

steps.title: The verse links entering a marriage to leaving one
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק places ״וְיָצְאָה״ next to ״וְהָיְתָה״. This היקש teaches that just as agency works for leaving a marriage, it works for entering one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And she leaves... and she becomes [another man's wife]." It compares becoming married to leaving a marriage. Just as leaving can be done through a שליח, becoming married can also be done through a שליח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a היקש, a comparison the Torah itself makes by putting two things side by side in one פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary comparison could be rejected because of the difference that she can be divorced against her will. A היקש, though, comes straight from the פסוק, so that difference does not stop it. Because of this, whatever works for יציאה (leaving a marriage) also works for הוויה (entering one), including a שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison the Torah makes by placing two things together; 'it compares'

steps.whatToRemember: Agency for a גט comes from ״וְשִׁלַּח / וְשִׁלְּחָהּ״. Agency for קידושין comes from the היקש of ״וְיָצְאָה״ to ״וְהָיְתָה״.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And she leaves... and she becomes"
it compares becoming married to leaving a marriage:
just as for leaving one can appoint an agent,
so too for becoming married one can appoint an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 with a היקש, which gets around the difference that a divorce can happen against her will.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש between ״וְיָצְאָה״ and ״וְהָיְתָה״ applies the agency rule of גירושין to קידושין.

steps.title: Bringing up the משנה about an agent separating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: an agent separating תרומה follows the owner's way of thinking, and if he does not know it, he gives one-fiftieth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what we learned in a משנה: If someone says to his agent, "Go separate תרומה," the agent separates according to the owner's way of thinking. If he does not know the owner's way of thinking, he separates a middle amount, one-fiftieth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה about a שליח for תרומה. This is a setup line: the actual question comes next, which is how we know that agency works for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, the sources for agency covered only גירושין and קידושין. This משנה shows that agency also works for תרומה, so the גמרא is preparing to ask for a source for that too.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
But what about what we learned in a משנה?

phrases.english: But what about that which we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in תרומות, chapter 4.

phrases.english: One who says to his agent: "Go separate תרומה"
the agent separates according to the owner's way of thinking.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ דַּעַת בַּעַל הַבַּיִת –
phrases.english: And if he does not know the owner's way of thinking,
he separates a middle amount, one-fiftieth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding sources for agency in גירושין and קידושין, the גמרא turns to agency for תרומה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setting up a question: where is the source that agency works for תרומה?
